learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the brilliant art of identifying what customers need, creating value, and delivering it better than the competition!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Selling focuses on the needs of the seller (pushing the product). Marketing focuses on the needs of the buyer (creating what the customer wants).

1. Production (cheap/available), 2. Product (high quality), 3. Selling (aggressive promotion), 4. Marketing (customer satisfaction), 5. Societal Marketing (customer satisfaction + environmental/social welfare).
The tools used to achieve marketing objectives: Product (what you sell), Price (what it costs), Place (distribution/where it's sold), and Promotion (advertising/communication).
Branding gives identity (name/logo). Packaging protects the product and acts as a 'silent salesman'. Labeling provides information required by law (ingredients, MRP, expiry).
Includes Advertising (paid, non-personal), Personal Selling (face-to-face), Sales Promotion (short-term incentives like 'Buy 1 Get 1'), and Public Relations (managing public image).

fun_activity.title: 👟 Design the Ultimate Sneaker
fun_activity.instructions: Invent a new sneaker! Define the 4 Ps: Product (What's special about it?), Price (How much?), Place (Online or exclusive stores?), and Promotion (Which celebrity will endorse it?).

exam_tips: 📌 Do not confuse the Marketing concept with the Societal Marketing concept. Societal includes ecological and ethical considerations.
📌 Remember that Packaging has three levels: Primary (tube of toothpaste), Secondary (cardboard box), and Transportation (large corrugated boxes).
📌 Public Relations (PR) is highly credible because the message comes in the form of news or articles, not a paid ad.
quick_recap: ⭐ Price is the only element in the marketing mix that generates revenue; the rest involve costs.
⭐ A Brand Mark is the part of a brand that can be recognized but not spoken (like the Nike Swoosh).
⭐ Sales Promotion techniques are meant to provide immediate, short-term boosts to sales.
